An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf retr 39.2
div.ab: Et laudatum est regi, quatinus consuetudines iustas et sapienter deductas non auferret eis, tantum in foro regio empto mercato suo cum testibus et cognitione uendentium.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 670 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.
The starred note (*) is printed across the whole page; it is given here, with the end of the Retractator’s text.
This is the last clause of ECf retr. Liebermann’s Anhang on pp. 670–672 (the chapter list of ‘Rubricator II’) is not yet added.

note.seg: d. i. Verfasser (unter Wilhelms I. Maske?), nicht die angebliche Angelsächs. Jury von 1070 im Prolog und 34, 1
i.e. the author (in the mask of William I?), not the alleged Anglo-Saxon jury of 1070 in the Prologue and 34, 1
bestehen bleiben die älteren drei Cautelen seit Hl 16, vor Einführung der Gewährbürgen: auf offenem Markt, mit Kaufzeugen und nicht ohne die Verkäufer zu kennen
the three older safeguards, in force since Hl 16, before the introduction of warrantor-sureties, remain: in the open market, with witnesses to the purchase, and not without knowing the sellers
Ablat. absol.: wenn nur ihr Einkauf auf öffentlichem Markt gekauft war
ablative absolute: provided only that their purchase was bought in the public market

Et concessum est fügt Texthand nachträglich zu Cb; folgt De latronibus, oben c. 36, Lond; folgt Geneal. Normann. Cb Oh Pe Hy Ld 1 Cu Hv Lb Ra Vi Rc Va La Ba Ph; über Gr vgl. u. S. 672b; Expliciunt leges sancti Edwardi, primo adinuente per Edgarum, auum suum, et per Willelmum conquestorem Anglie confirmate et prius tempore Cnutonis regis approbate fügt zu Db L [Erwähnung Cnuts widerspricht ECf. 34, 1b; 3, aber vgl. S. 618f]

the text hand adds Et concessum est later in Cb; De latronibus, above c. 36, follows in Lond; the Geneal. Normann. follows in Cb Oh Pe Hy Ld 1 Cu Hv Lb Ra Vi Rc Va La Ba Ph; on Gr cf. below, p. 672, note b; Db L add Expliciunt leges sancti Edwardi, primo adinuente per Edgarum, auum suum, et per Willelmum conquestorem Anglie confirmate et prius tempore Cnutonis regis approbate [the mention of Cnut contradicts ECf 34, 1b; 3, but cf. p. 618, note f]

div.ab: And it was recommended to the king that he should not take away from them the customs, just and wisely derived, only [that] their purchase be bought [?] in the royal market with witnesses and with the knowledge of the sellers.
